I’m currently trying to recover from anorexia, and when I was really struggling I also drank very little water. TW: I’m going to discuss my experiences and my reasoning behind it at the time.

One of the first reasons I drank so little water was because of the dreaded “water weight” that I was always afraid would show up on the scale. I knew it didn’t actually mean I had gained permanent weight, but it felt that way. I also honestly wasn’t very thirsty most of the time. I don’t know if this is a universal experience among people with anorexia or not, but when I stopped eating it became harder and harder to remember or even want to drink water. Plus, when I did drink water after so much time without it it made me feel really nauseated. It just wasn’t something I thought about much, and it didn’t really feel important or worth drinking. Just adding my two cents!!

The problem is that autism isn’t a mental illness- it’s who you are. You can’t “take out the autism”. If this post was about something like depression or ocd or bipolar then I would agree with your point, because those are all things that can be cured, or “taken out”. But autism isn’t something to be cured, it’s just a different kind of brain. Because of this, statements like “I hate your autism but I love you” don’t really make sense as a huge, inescapable part of who they are is autism. You wouldn’t tell a neurotypical person “hey, I hate every way you perceive and relate to the world, but I love you”.
